title: DSPy Streaming Module
summary: This module provides core functionalities for streaming outputs from DSPy programs, allowing incremental results and status updates. It includes tools to wrap programs for streaming, listen for specific output fields, and format streams for external APIs.

nodes.label: Wrap DSPy Program for Streaming
nodes.title: Wrap DSPy Program for Streaming
nodes.description: This component transforms a standard DSPy program into a streaming version, enabling it to yield incremental outputs and status messages. It supports both asynchronous and synchronous execution modes, providing flexibility for various application needs. Users can configure custom status message providers and stream listeners to tailor the streaming behavior.

nodes.label: Provide Synchronous Stream Interface
nodes.title: Provide Synchronous Stream Interface
nodes.description: This utility function converts an asynchronous DSPy program stream into a synchronous generator. It allows users to consume streaming outputs in environments that do not natively support async iterators, simplifying integration into existing synchronous codebases.

nodes.label: Format Stream for OpenAI API
nodes.title: Format Stream for OpenAI API
nodes.description: This component takes DSPy's internal streaming output and converts it into an OpenAI-compatible Server-Sent Events (SSE) format. It's designed for use in API responses, allowing DSPy programs to serve streaming results that adhere to common industry standards.

nodes.label: Extract Specific Field from Stream
nodes.title: Extract Specific Field from Stream
nodes.description: This class acts as an observer for streaming outputs, specifically designed to identify and extract content related to a designated signature field from a predictor's output. It intelligently handles various adapter types like Chat, JSON, and XML for accurate parsing and buffering of stream chunks.

nodes.label: Execute Function in New Async Loop
nodes.title: Execute Function in New Async Loop
nodes.description: This utility creates and manages a new asyncio event loop to run a given asynchronous function in an isolated environment. It ensures that async operations can proceed independently, preventing conflicts with existing event loops and providing a clean execution context.

nodes.label: Original DSPy Program
nodes.title: Original DSPy Program
nodes.description: Represents the core DSPy program or module that is being enhanced with streaming capabilities. This is the input to the streamification process, which then produces incremental outputs.

nodes.label: DSPy Asynchronous Stream
nodes.title: DSPy Asynchronous Stream
nodes.description: The incremental output stream generated by a streamified DSPy program. This is typically an async generator that yields `StreamResponse` objects or `Prediction` instances as the program executes.

nodes.label: OpenAI-Compatible SSE Stream
nodes.title: OpenAI-Compatible SSE Stream
nodes.description: The final output stream formatted as Server-Sent Events (SSE), designed to be compatible with OpenAI's API streaming response format. This stream can be directly served as an API response.

nodes.label: Language Model Stream Chunks
nodes.title: Language Model Stream Chunks
nodes.description: Raw, incremental text or data chunks received directly from a Language Model during a streaming completion. These chunks are processed by stream listeners to extract relevant information.

groups.label: Surface Components
groups.title: User-Facing Streaming Interfaces
groups.description: These components provide the primary interfaces for users to enable and manage streaming functionalities within DSPy programs.

groups.label: Generative Components
groups.title: Stream Generation & Execution
groups.description: Components responsible for orchestrating the generation of streaming outputs or managing the execution context for such operations.

groups.label: Analytical Components
groups.title: Stream Content Analysis
groups.description: Components that analyze and process the content of incoming data streams to extract specific information or apply transformations.

groups.label: Data Entities
groups.title: Data Flow & External Interactions
groups.description: Represents the various data inputs, outputs, and external systems involved in the streaming process.
